name: Land & ecology
tagline: The ground everything depends on.
summary: Establish the land, water rights, ecological conditions, and resource base that can support the entire network. The ecosystem may span several locations; each location needs a clear purpose, carrying-capacity assessment, and restoration responsibility.
build: Map soil, water, hazards, biodiversity, and resource deposits.
Match activities to suitable sites and establish legitimate access.
Measure depletion, regeneration, and ecological impacts over time.
replacement: Land cannot be treated as a consumable that is infinitely replaceable. Preserve soil, habitat, and resource quality across the planning horizon.
proof: Show that intended demand fits measured resource availability, approved use, and a funded stewardship plan.

name: Water & sanitation
tagline: A complete water cycle.
summary: Supply drinking, agricultural, clinical, and industrial water through distinct quality pathways. Connect storage and distribution to wastewater collection, treatment, appropriate reuse, and safe residual handling. Every downstream service depends on reliable water quality.
build: Characterize source quality, demand, and seasonal availability.
Build treatment, storage, distribution, and sanitation capacity.
Verify water quality, outage response, and appropriate reuse.
replacement: Trace pipes, valves, pump motors, membranes, treatment chemistry, and calibration equipment back to their producers.
proof: Meet the declared water specifications under peak demand and an equipment outage, with losses and external treatment inputs disclosed.

name: Energy & power
tagline: Generate. Store. Distribute. Recover.
summary: Create the electrical and thermal backbone for homes, farms, clinics, factories, and transport. Generation, storage, distribution, heating, and cooling must operate as a coordinated system that can recover from interruptions and support critical loads.
build: Define demand profiles and prioritize essential loads.
Qualify generation, storage, distribution, and control systems.
Demonstrate outage isolation, recovery, and dependable output.
replacement: Account for cells, conductors, switchgear, inverters, lubricants, and replacement generation equipment. Owning panels does not produce the next panel.
proof: Demonstrate energy adequacy by time period and contingency, including equipment replacement and conversion losses.

name: Agriculture & seeds
tagline: Food independence starts before the farm.
summary: Produce a suitable mix of staple foods, fresh foods, feed, and biological inputs. Agriculture includes seed renewal, soil fertility, propagation, appropriate animal systems, and the machinery needed to sustain output through different seasons.
build: Define the nutrition basket and choose suitable production systems.
Establish seed, water, nutrient, and equipment pathways.
Measure seasonal yields, crop losses, feed needs, and storage.
replacement: Reproduce seed and critical farm equipment while tracking nutrient losses. Recovered materials require appropriate quality before agricultural reuse.
proof: Supply the agreed food basket through representative seasons, with feed, fertilizers, seed, and machinery dependencies recorded.

name: Food processing
tagline: Turn harvests into dependable nutrition.
summary: Connect agricultural output to safe, usable food through processing, kitchens, preservation, storage, packaging, and distribution. Capacity must match seasonal harvests as well as everyday demand, with traceable lots and an effective recall process.
outputs: Qualified supplies for stores and kitchens
build: Select processing methods for the agreed food basket.
Establish sanitation, quality testing, and cold-chain controls.
Connect production schedules, storage, distribution, and recalls.
replacement: Include compressors, refrigeration materials, processing machinery, cleaning supplies, and food-contact packaging in the dependency graph.
proof: Deliver accepted food with measured yield, spoilage, storage conditions, and complete origin-to-store traceability.

name: Grocery & essentials
tagline: Our stores. A complete supply chain.
summary: Operate Saber grocery stores and household-essential outlets with clear prices, accessible service, dependable stock, and pickup or delivery. Stores are the member-facing end of a larger food, manufacturing, warehousing, and logistics system.
build: Define the basket, service promise, and transparent price basis.
Operate receiving, stock control, recalls, and substitutions.
Connect household demand to internal production and distribution.
replacement: Trace each stocked item to ingredients and manufacturing inputs. Purchasing from a company-owned distributor alone does not close the dependency.
proof: Keep the agreed basket available at its stated quality, while identifying every externally sourced item and disclosed subsidy.

name: Fuel & charging
tagline: Own the station. Trace the energy.
summary: Operate fuel stations, storage, metering, charging, and fleet access. The long-term production model follows each energy carrier upstream to its source, processing, quality controls, distribution, and the equipment that sustains it. A proposed used-cooking-oil recovery connection can supply qualified biodiesel production; plastic and aluminum are not biodiesel feedstocks.
build: Identify which uses require liquid fuel and which can electrify.
Design supply, storage, distribution, and station operations.
Qualify upstream production pathways and their full input needs.
replacement: Fuel processing has feedstock, catalyst, energy, equipment, and environmental dependencies. Charging also depends on power electronics and vehicle batteries.
proof: Demonstrate accepted fuel or electrical supply with complete origin, loss, maintenance, and replenishment records.

name: Housing & community
tagline: A place to live. A system built to last.
summary: Provide accessible homes for different household needs, supported by utilities, maintenance, community spaces, and orderly tenancy arrangements. Housing includes the continuing ability to renovate and replace buildings, rather than only the first construction project.
build: Define household needs, building types, accessibility, and service standards.
Connect construction, utilities, occupancy, and maintenance records.
Fund repairs, renewal, and practical transition arrangements.
replacement: Follow roofs, glazing, fixtures, heat pumps, wiring, appliances, and structural materials to qualified production and repair pathways.
proof: Show that households receive the promised housing quality and continuity, with maintenance capacity and replacement obligations funded.

name: Human healthcare
tagline: Care with independent clinical authority.
summary: Build a coordinated care system covering primary, dental, vision, mental, chronic, urgent, and specialist needs within a declared service scope. Professional operators own clinical decisions and records; Protect coordinates access and program terms.
build: Define covered services and explicit advanced-care dependencies.
Establish clinical staffing, supplies, records, and quality oversight.
Verify the patient journey, result follow-up, emergency response, and downtime care.
replacement: Trace medicines, sterile consumables, medical gases, diagnostic reagents, equipment parts, and calibration. Necessary external care remains available while gaps are open.
proof: Qualified professionals accept the supported care pathways and continuity arrangements. A clinic building alone cannot establish complete medical independence.

name: Medicines & diagnostics
tagline: The industrial foundation of care.
summary: Develop pharmacy operations and qualified production pathways for selected medicines, consumables, diagnostic materials, and medical technology. Manufacturing scope must follow actual clinical needs and maintain independent quality functions.
build: Define a formulary and the required clinical supply catalogue.
Map ingredients, process equipment, testing, and packaging.
Qualify each production and quality pathway before use.
replacement: Include analytical instruments, sterile equipment, reagents, high-purity inputs, packaging, and the tools required to maintain them.
proof: Establish product-specific quality, capacity, authorization, and continuity evidence. Internal manufacture is a capability to qualify, not an exemption from standards.

name: Nexus education
tagline: Develop the people who sustain the system.
summary: Connect childhood and adult education with trades, professional development, research, apprenticeships, and leadership succession. Nexus supports accountable learning; a reviewed curriculum and qualified assessment turn participation into demonstrated capability.
build: Define learning and workforce needs for each operating domain.
Deliver complete admission-to-learning-to-assessment journeys.
Connect supervised practice, qualification, and continuing development.
replacement: Preserve teaching capability, course lineage, practical equipment, and qualified successors. A course-title inventory does not establish released education.
proof: Learners complete accepted work and assessment, while operators can demonstrate the competencies required for their responsibilities.

name: Family & community life
tagline: A complete life beyond the workplace.
summary: Include childcare, elder support, disability access, recreation, fitness, arts, libraries, social support, and appropriate end-of-life services. Community infrastructure must support different household circumstances and preserve independent choices.
build: Define service needs across ages and household circumstances.
Appoint qualified operators and establish access and continuity.
Provide independent feedback, complaints, and practical alternatives.
replacement: Maintain facilities, equipment, and the workforce that supplies care. Continuity depends on people and qualified successors as much as physical assets.
proof: Demonstrate safe, accessible services with staffed capacity, clear terms, and effective response to changing needs.

name: Champion veterinary
tagline: Animal health, professionally governed.
summary: Provide veterinary operations through Champion, keeping animal patients, practice workflows, clinical authority, and treatment funding distinct from human care. Where the food system includes animals, qualified animal-health capacity becomes an upstream dependency.
build: Define supported practice and animal-care scope.
Verify encounters, estimates, treatment, supplies, and follow-up.
Reconcile any treatment funds under their actual restrictions.
replacement: Trace veterinary medicines, laboratory equipment, clinical supplies, and practice-system maintenance to qualified sources.
proof: A responsible practice accepts the complete care workflow, including records, financial reconciliation, support, and recovery.

name: Transport & logistics
tagline: Connect every physical promise.
summary: Move people, food, materials, equipment, and finished goods through reliable freight, passenger transport, warehousing, cold-chain, and maintenance operations. STLoads and Saber TMS retain distinct marketplace and execution responsibilities.
build: Map demand, routes, storage, and appropriate transport modes.
Coordinate readiness, assignment, execution, and exceptions.
Verify delivery, reconciliation, recovery, and fleet maintenance.
replacement: Include tires, batteries, drivetrains, brakes, vehicle electronics, and depot equipment. Internal dispatch is not internal vehicle manufacture.
proof: Complete demand-to-delivery journeys under stated conditions with actual field evidence, accepted exceptions, and qualified fleet continuity.

name: Construction & trades
tagline: Build it. Maintain it. Build the next one.
summary: Develop civil works, building trades, fabrication, inspection, renovation, and preventive maintenance. Shared expertise can support several operators while each asset keeps a named owner, service standard, and maintenance obligation.
build: Define design standards and accountable asset responsibilities.
Develop trades, supply pathways, tools, and quality acceptance.
Connect commissioning to maintenance and lifecycle renewal.
replacement: Track construction machinery, specialized tools, measurement equipment, consumables, and the industrial capacity to reproduce them.
proof: Qualified review accepts completed assets and demonstrates the ability to maintain them at the promised service level.

name: Materials & chemistry
tagline: Move upstream to the material itself.
summary: Supply metals, timber, aggregates, binders, glass, ceramics, polymers, industrial gases, and appropriate process chemicals. Each selected pathway requires suitable resources, energy, water, skilled operation, quality control, and responsible residual handling.
build: Identify the material specifications required by actual products.
Map deposits, renewable feedstocks, recovery, and production routes.
Qualify yield, quality, resource limits, and environmental responsibilities.
replacement: Process plants need catalysts, refractory materials, corrosion-resistant parts, controls, and replacement equipment. Include these in the same upstream analysis.
proof: Produce accepted material at required capacity with measured losses, energy, resource depletion, and remaining outside inputs.

name: Machinery & manufacturing
tagline: The capacity to replace productive capacity.
summary: Build the machine-shop, fabrication, foundry, motor, pump, component, and industrial-equipment capabilities required by the wider system. Precision, quality assurance, tooling, and measurement must match each intended application.
build: Inventory critical assets and their bills of materials.
Qualify repair, fabrication, and manufacturing pathways.
Extend analysis to the machinery that makes the machinery.
replacement: Bearings, seals, cutting tools, lubricants, instruments, and control components are often hidden dependencies. Track them explicitly.
proof: Demonstrate critical replacement parts and equipment against accepted specifications, including upstream tools and production capacity.

name: Electronics & communications
tagline: Expose the dependencies inside the device.
summary: Cover sensors, controls, power electronics, network equipment, computing, communications, and their maintenance. Repair and assembly can precede deeper manufacturing, but semiconductor and specialist-tool dependencies remain visible until qualified internal routes exist.
build: Define the minimum required device and communications catalogue.
Establish repair, test, assembly, and suitable substitution pathways.
Trace high-purity materials, chips, and fabrication-tool dependencies.
replacement: A self-hosted server still needs chips, storage, power supplies, and cooling. Chip fabrication has its own demanding upstream equipment and material requirements.
proof: Qualify supported hardware and replacement pathways, while separating local operation from externally governed global connectivity.

name: Clothing & household goods
tagline: Everyday essentials, made maintainable.
summary: Produce and repair clothing, footwear, furniture, appliances, personal-care goods, and cleaning supplies. Define a practical household basket with quality, accessibility, durability, and repair requirements rather than an undefined promise to manufacture everything.
build: Define household product specifications and demand.
Connect raw materials, manufacturing, repair, and distribution.
Measure durability, material losses, and replacement needs.
replacement: Include textile machinery, appliance electronics, dyes, cleaning inputs, footwear components, and production tools in upstream analysis.
proof: Supply the agreed household basket with verified quality and repair support, identifying all externally sourced ingredients and components.

name: Recovery & environment
tagline: Recover value. Account for what is lost.
summary: Connect a recycling plant, waste-management operation, and compost/mulch facility. Recover paving inputs, soil products, plastics, metals, and glass; route used cooking oil toward qualified biodiesel production. Every stream needs an accepted output and accountable residual handling.
inputs: Processing assets, energy, water, and qualified operators
Quality specifications and confirmed receiving uses
outputs: Qualified paving, material, compost, and mulch inputs
A defined oil-recovery connection to fuel production
Measured recovery, rejects, and residual destinations
build: Design recycling, collection/transfer, and compost/mulch operations within the community upkeep plan.
Qualify each material pathway; keep plastic-derived fuel distinct from biodiesel and aluminum in the metals loop.
Record mass balance, output acceptance, maintenance, actual costs, and remaining outside dependencies.
replacement: Recovery facilities require their own machinery, consumables, and safe maintenance. Recycling does not remove every need for new material.
proof: Reconcile each material stream and demonstrate that recovered output meets the next process specification without hiding losses.

name: Finance & risk
tagline: Keep obligations as visible as ambition.
summary: Coordinate payroll, accounting, capital allocation, payments, appropriate credit and savings access, insurance arrangements, and assistance. Separate each company's obligations and restricted funds while making shared-service costs and subsidies understandable.
build: Identify funding entities, custody, restrictions, and authority.
Connect physical costs, operating capacity, and cash plans.
Test downside cases and fund maintenance and continuity.
replacement: Internal payments do not create additional goods or cash. Financial interfaces and public obligations remain explicit even as physical purchases decline.
proof: Reconcile cash and commitments, disclose subsidies, and demonstrate that the next service obligation has an authorized funding path.

name: Safety & continuity
tagline: Essential services must survive disruption.
summary: Provide accountable incident management, fire prevention and response, emergency coordination, disaster planning, physical and cyber protection, and recovery exercises. Plan for simultaneous failures and the absence of critical personnel.
build: Define essential services, hazards, and incident authority.
Prepare local continuity, backups, response, and external interfaces.
Run representative drills and verify corrections.
replacement: Emergency supplies, protective equipment, communications, and qualified successors also require replenishment and maintenance pathways.
proof: Demonstrate recovery against agreed service requirements, with real evidence rather than the presence of a written plan alone.

name: Governance & operations
tagline: Clear authority. Independent accountability.
summary: Connect Saber Tech portfolio stewardship, operator mandates, Axiom community participation, professional governance, independent appeals, and enterprise operations. Every consequential decision needs a legitimate owner and a reviewable record.
build: Separate corporate, community, professional, and household authority.
Define delegated powers, conflicts, reviews, and execution receipts.
Test acting authority and decisions during founder absence.
replacement: Maintain institutional knowledge, acting authority, independent reviewers, and successors. A title or software role alone cannot create real authority.
proof: Show that responsible operators can act, members can challenge decisions, and essential work continues without personal intervention from the founder.

name: Aether digital backbone
tagline: One coordinated experience. Accountable domains.
summary: Use Aether for access and workspaces, ATMP-CORE for reusable mechanisms, and independent domain systems for authoritative records. The digital layer coordinates the physical ecosystem through asset, production, dependency, and evidence records.
build: Establish entity, operator, authority, asset, and service registries.
Connect domain-owned workflows through explicit contracts.
Verify permissions, persistence, reconciliation, and recovery.
replacement: Track hosting, licenses, model services, firmware, hardware, and build-tool dependencies. Offline essential operations need explicit procedures.
proof: Complete accepted user journeys on an identified release, with cross-domain permissions enforced and recovery demonstrated.
